subject: general
question: The standard deviation of the first 10 natural numbers is 3.028. What will be the standard deviation of the first 20 natural numbers?
solution:
The correct answer is **5.845**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**The standard deviation of the first 10 natural numbers: 

Formula: σ = sqrt {{(n² - 1)}over 12}; where, σ = standard deviation, n = sample size 

Or, σ = sqrt{(20² - 1) over 12} = 5.766 approx 5.8

This is closest to 5.845 

**Hence, the standard deviation of the first 20 natural numbers is 5.845.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__** The standard deviation of a set of numbers is a measure of the amount of variance or dispersion among the numbers. It doesn't scale linearly or predictably with the number of elements in the set, or with the standard deviation of a different set of numbers. Therefore, the standard deviation of the first 20 natural numbers can't be calculated directly from the standard deviation of the first 10 natural numbers.
